description:
pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs line 72: CertPool implements IntoIterator for &CertPool but does not expose an iter() method. Rust convention (and clippy::pedantic lint 'iter_without_into_iter') says that when you implement IntoIterator for a reference type, you should also provide an iter() method returning the same iterator type.

Without iter(), users who want to iterate must write either for c in &pool or pool.into_iter() — the latter being unusual for references. The idiomatic &pool.iter() pattern does not compile.

Fix: add pub fn iter(&self) -> core::slice::Iter<'_, x509_cert::Certificate> to CertPool that delegates to self.certs.iter().

Clippy pedantic fires: 'IntoIterator implemented for a reference type without an iter method'
title: CertPool: IntoIterator for &CertPool missing companion iter() method
